headline: NEW, SUPERSEDES Vance-letter standing -- Trump denies directing Vance peace letter to Iran
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM + CONTESTED SUB-CLAIM] VP JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, testing a framework for negotiations. WSJ, citing a person familiar with the matter, says it was sent at Trump's direction.
sources: Wall Street Journal (Vance letter report); Donald Trump remarks to reporters at Joint Base Andrews; Abbas Araghchi X post; Axios via US official (nuclear-stress detail)
fault_line: Talks or trap? Is the Vance letter a genuine off-ramp, or a medical-supplies cover while a short, intense post-midterm strike is readied?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM + CONTESTED SUB-CLAIM] VP JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, testing a framework for negotiations. WSJ, citing a person familiar with the matter, says it was sent at Trump's direction. Trump denied directing peace talks: 'No. Iran needs help with medical supplies. Basically, it is getting supplies in to help people that are not well.' Trump separately acknowledged approving Vance's contact (per Bloomberg via The Statesman). Axios, citing a US official, says Vance's letter stressed any talks to halt potential US strikes would 'require discussions on the nuclear issue'; Vance said Trump was 'enthusiastic about' the letter (per Jerusalem Post/Axios). Araghchi: Iran is in 'close and ongoing contact with intermediaries' to implement its 7-day plan 'in even less than a week'; plan sequence per published accounts: US ends hostilities, lifts naval blockade on Iranian ports, eases oil-export curbs, releases frozen assets (days 1-5), Iran reopens Hormuz to normal shipping (day 6), wider talks resume (day 7). A separate Qatar compromise draft (7-day gradual exchange + IAEA-access-for-sanctions-easing) is reported by Aju Press citing Reuters, with Iran reportedly negative toward the new Qatari proposal -- Aju is NOT in the source registry and this sub-claim is attribution-only.
sections.what_verified: 3 declared families: WSJ T2 (letter + at-Trump's-direction sourcing) + Axios T2 (nuclear-stress detail, via Jerusalem Post T3 carrying Axios) + Times of India T3 (denial quote + Araghchi statement + letter). The letter's EXISTENCE and Trump's reframing are strongly supported (primary quotes, multiple carriers). The letter's PURPOSE/DIRECTION is contested: WSJ sourcing vs Trump's own denial -- unresolved.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's own denial contradicts WSJ's 'at Trump's direction' sourcing on purpose (not on contact itself -- contact is confirmed by Trump). Rezaei said last week Tehran will not negotiate until core demands are met. AP (via The Week) reported US officials urging regional allies to prepare for possible renewed strikes after the Nov 3 midterms -- the strike track runs in parallel with the letter track. CENTCOM denied Iranian claims of commercial vessels hitting Hormuz sea mines, saying primary transit routes 'have been cleared of sea mines by US forces and remain so' (via Newscord summary -- CENTCOM T1 claim, attributed).
sections.why_matters: Trump denies his own peace channel: the letter exists, the purpose is now the fight. Lead with Trump's own denial quote vs the WSJ sourcing, then the 7-day Hormuz sequence and the Nov 3 hinge. Counted Hormuz transits remain near zero on the last (stale) PortWatch observation -- never present claimant figures as counted.
